title: ESXi management network menu
note: Actual vendor ESXi 8.0.3 screen. VLAN is highlighted in the source; use IPv4 and DNS entries for their own settings. It does not show a successfully configured management connection. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: IPv4 configuration: enter only the planned management address.
DNS configuration: use your approved name and DNS servers.
Read the actual ESXi release and build at the bottom.

title: Read the exact Add Host precheck error
note: Vendor error example involving old ESXi 7 versions, not a recommended combination or a successful add-host result. License warnings and source redactions are preserved. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: Confirm the selected inventory object.
Read the expanded host/lifecycle compatibility failure.
Use Recent Tasks for the failed operation and its details.

title: Recognize the standard-switch uplink warning
note: The published warning overlays adapter selection. No active uplink can mean intentional same-host isolation or an incomplete external path. Never move a management uplink to imitate this image. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: The wizard is creating a standard switch.
Unclaimed is not the same as Active.
Read the warning and verify the intended isolation or uplink design.

title: Inspect existing partitions before any format
platform: ESXi shell partition listing · build not stated in source image
note: This is a vendor shell-output screenshot, not the Host Client. It shows existing partitions in a missing-datastore diagnosis; it is NOT a blank disk or an instruction to erase it. No shell command execution is required in this class. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: The command targets a specific storage device; do not copy it.
Existing partition records require an ownership check.

title: Locate a VM disk and its datastore
platform: vSphere Client Edit Settings · historical vendor reference; exact build unstated
note: Vendor example shows VM_deploy and an iscsi2 datastore. A bracketed datastore name and snapshot-backed disk file are visible. This is not a CloudSeam VM, a new VM recipe or a recommendation to alter the file. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: Expand the virtual disk to inspect its settings.
The bracketed name identifies the backing datastore.
The disk filename can indicate a snapshot-backed disk.

title: Check a VM network adapter connection
platform: VMware ESXi / vCenter Edit Settings · exact source build unstated
note: Official diagnostic example: Connected and Connect At Power On are unchecked. Published black redactions are unchanged. Do not copy its CPU, RAM, disk or network values. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: Expand the intended network adapter and confirm its backing.
Connected describes the current virtual cable state.
Connect At Power On controls the next boot.

title: Recognize installer-media connection settings
platform: VMware VM CD/DVD settings · exact source build unstated
note: Official diagnostic example shows Host Device and unavailable media, not a selected installation ISO. The lesson requires the approved datastore ISO during install and disconnection after it is no longer needed. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: Connected describes the current virtual CD/DVD connection.
Connect At Power On controls boot-time connection.
Inspect the actual media backing; this example is unavailable.

title: Read Manage Snapshots before acting
platform: vSphere Client Manage Snapshots · historical July 2020 example; exact build unstated
note: Source shows a memory-enabled snapshot of VM_deploy. Our first exercise uses a cleanly powered-off disposable VM. Memory and quiescing values in this screenshot are examples, not settings to copy. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: The tree lists the snapshot and current position.
Delete removes a checkpoint; it is not Revert.
Revert returns to the selected snapshot state.

title: Recognize a snapshot-backed disk filename
platform: vSphere Client Edit Settings · historical vendor reference; exact build unstated
note: Source highlights a virtual disk filename ending in -000001.vmdk. This is snapshot-chain evidence only. Never delete, rename or edit disk-chain files by hand. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: The selected device is a virtual disk, not a physical host disk.
The bracketed part is the datastore.
A numbered VMDK may be snapshot-backed; preserve the full chain.

title: Find the vCenter appliance backup page
note: Vendor page shows no configured schedule and no listed jobs. This is a starting state, not proof of protection. VAMI protects the appliance configuration/database, not all application VM disks. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: Backup is an appliance-management page.
Configure creates the backup schedule.
Backup Now starts a separate on-demand job.

title: Verify the appliance backup activity
platform: vCenter Server 8.0 VAMI · official historical backup example
note: Vendor example shows a completed job and published redactions. It is not our backup result. Confirm your own timestamp, destination files and isolated restore test separately. Original retained unchanged; numbered overlay and reading key added by CloudSeam Tech.

markers.label: Check the actual job state, not just schedule creation.
Review transfer size and duration for the job.
Verify the intended destination and corresponding files.
